title: Payment SDKs, Tokenization, and Tap-to-pay Boundaries

scout.purpose: Master payment sdks, tokenization, and tap-to-pay boundaries through a production or platform contract supported by causal evidence.
scout.realWorldUse: Specialist Android work must remain compatible, secure, measurable, accessible, distributable, and operable outside a demonstration.
scout.outcome: You can design, inspect, test, release, and defend payment sdks, tokenization, and tap-to-pay boundaries.

blocks.text: A payment SDK is an orchestrated boundary, not the authority that moves money. The app presents amount and merchant context, a provider returns tokenized payment data, and a trusted backend or gateway verifies, authorizes, captures, refunds, and reconciles under idempotent operation IDs. Direct handling of card data expands PCI DSS scope; gateway tokenization can reduce but not automatically eliminate obligations. Verify exact provider documentation, environment, merchant identity, signing, and production approval.

blocks.text: Google Pay payment data uses defined tokenization schemes and, for direct integrations, signed and encrypted protocol payloads requiring server verification and key management. Never decrypt or log payment credentials in the Android client. Amount, currency, merchant, cart, and transaction identity must be revalidated server-side. Tap-to-pay acceptance involves NFC, secure elements or kernels, network certification, device and merchant eligibility, and regional regulation; ordinary host card emulation is not a shortcut to a certified acceptance product.

blocks.caption: A focused fragment whose complete contract includes exact versions, ownership, adverse paths, compatibility, and release evidence.

blocks.text: Test readiness, cancellation, duplicate callback, timeout after authorization, process death, network loss, repeated tap, partial capture, refund, account switch, sandbox versus production, key rotation, provider outage, and reconciliation. Make submit idempotent and show pending until backend truth resolves. Redact logs and screenshots. Maintain certification evidence, dependency and key lifecycle, fraud monitoring, accessibility, and incident runbooks. Never infer success solely from a client callback.

Expert engineering makes assumptions, authority, compatibility, security, privacy, accessibility, performance, distribution, and recovery reviewable. Begin with a concrete user or platform outcome, identify trust and lifecycle boundaries, and retain exact source, dependency, toolchain, configuration, model or platform version, and artifact identity. Test realistic success plus denial, offline, process death, cancellation, corruption, version skew, resource pressure, and dependency failure. Measure representative distributions rather than best runs. Document unsupported cases, residual risk, owners, release gates, incident response, deprecation, and rollback or roll-forward. A specialised solution is production-ready only when another team can integrate, verify, operate, upgrade, disable, and remove it safely.

trap_check.mistake: Showing “paid” immediately after the client receives payment data can create false success when backend authorization times out or fails.
trap_check.why: It hides an ownership, compatibility, trust, lifecycle, or evidence gap that becomes costly outside the demonstration.
trap_check.fix: Make the disputed boundary explicit and add a representative negative or compatibility test plus operational response.

trap_check.mistake: Treating one successful device, client, model, platform build, or release as proof of the supported contract.
trap_check.why: Advanced Android ecosystems contain version, hardware, consumer, policy, and runtime variation.
trap_check.fix: Define the support matrix and verify exact artifacts across representative and adverse conditions.

challenge_intro.task: Model a Google Pay and conceptual tap-to-pay journey with tokenization, server pricing, idempotency, pending recovery, key lifecycle, PCI boundaries, and reconciliation.
challenge_intro.successLooksLike: The work includes a minimal coherent implementation, exact evidence, support and threat boundaries, adverse testing, release operation, and recovery.

recall.prompt: Why must the backend reprice the cart?
recall.answer: Client amount and cart data can be stale or tampered; the trusted authority must validate the transaction before authorization.

recall.prompt: What must accompany an expert Android artifact?
recall.answer: Exact source and build identity, supported versions, contracts, tests, measurements, security and privacy review, release evidence, owner, and recovery plan.
They prevent consumers and operators from treating an untested or impossible condition as a silent guarantee.
